summary: ARAM (Active Radar Analysis & Mapping) is a web app developed by team HoneyFIX for the “Dancing with the SARs” challenge. It takes Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data and turns it into clear 3D maps and visual insights that non-expert users can understand without radar-processing knowledge. SAR sees through clouds and at night, so it helps with tracking ground deformation in Mexicali, Baja California. ARAM matters because it makes slow, invisible ground sinking around Cerro Prieto visible, so people can see where the land is changing and how many people live nearby.

DANCING WITH THE SARs: FEATURES AND PRESENTATION GUIDE

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 | Mexicali Local Event | Challenge "Dancing with the SARs"

Base document for building the project presentation (maximum 7 slides, in English).

 

==========================================================================

1. THE PROJECT IN ONE SENTENCE

==========================================================================

An isometric 3D map of the Mexicali Valley where the user pilots a ship over the terrain and sees, with NISAR radar, how the ground changes over one year. The central case is the subsidence around the Cerro Prieto geothermal field.

 

DATA BEHIND IT

- Real NISAR measurements (PROVISIONAL products, October 2025 to October 2026).

- Copernicus DEM (relief), ESA WorldCover 2021 (land use), WorldPop 2020 (population) and OpenStreetMap (roads, canals and rivers).

 

HOW THE WORK IS SPLIT

- A Python pipeline, which runs offline, converts NISAR and the relief data into static files.

- The web app only reads those files. It does not process radar and does not need NASA Earthdata credentials.

 

==========================================================================

2. PROJECT FEATURES (in presentation language)

==========================================================================

This section explains what each feature does and what it is for, without code.

 

2.1 Flight over the valley

- The user steers a ship with the keyboard (WASD) or by touch, over an isometric camera.

- There are preset destinations (Cerro Prieto, Mexicali, the river) and an animated jump between regions.

- What it is for: exploring the valley as a place, not as a data table.

 

2.2 Timeline

- Play and pause button, and a date slider. Playback advances one date every 3 seconds and returns to the start when it ends.

- The date appears as a large headline, with the elapsed time in words ("at 8 months").

- What it is for: watching the ground change move through time.

 

2.3 Ground-motion views

Only one view is active at a time.

 

VIEW | WHAT IT SHOWS | WHAT IT IS FOR

---------------|------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------

Accumulated | How much the ground has moved up to the chosen date | Watching the subsidence bowl grow

Rate | Rate of change in cm per year, summarizing the whole series| Comparing fast and slow zones

Zones | Areas of subsidence or uplift of at least 1 km2, in bands | Going from the pixel to "zones that matter"

Differential | Where the change is sharpest (cm per km) | Pointing out edges and gradients

Acceleration | Whether the rate rose or fell between the first and second | Seeing whether subsidence speeds up or slows

| half of the year | down (requires at least 4 dates)

 

Zone bands: high (<= -10 cm), medium (<= -5 cm), low (<= -2 cm) and uplift (>= +2 cm).

 

2.4 Surface, water and impact layers

- Surface: radar intensity (HH and HV), surface change and moisture of the top few centimeters of soil.

- Water: permanent water and new water by date, with decorative waves that can be turned off.

- Impact: how many people (WorldPop) and what land use (WorldCover) are inside each zone. It counts exposure, not damage.

- What it is for: connecting the radar data with people and territory.

 

2.5 Ship dashboard and probe

- What lies under the ship is translated into words: trend (stable, slow, moderate or fast), a size comparison ("like a pencil", "like a hand"), heading, speed in km/h and the nearest point of interest.

- What it is for: "flying is measuring". A technical value is understood without reading a scale.

 

2.6 Inspector

- Tapping the map reads the value of all layers at that point.

- What it is for: answering "what does the data say about this place?".

 

2.7 Events

- A catalog of measured changes, grouped by type, with a shortcut to the largest one. When one is selected, the ship flies there and the map opens the layer and the date that detected it.

- What it is for: telling the story without the audience having to search.

 

2.8 Crops and water

- Splits the agricultural zones (WorldCover 2021) into listable areas, shows soil moisture by date, allows comparing up to 3 zones and flags whether a canal or river lies within 2 km.

- It does not name the crop, does not estimate harvest and does not treat proximity to water as irrigation.

- What it is for: showing the agricultural valley as context for the subsidence.

 

2.9 Illustrative 3D subsidence

- Exaggerates the relief x2,000, x5,000 or x10,000 so the change can be seen in 3D. It is an illustration. The real data is in the layers, not in the exaggeration.

 

2.10 Transparency and accessibility

- "?" help with the limit of each layer, a data provenance notice, a context panel about SAR and InSAR, and credits.

- Settings for visibility, opacity, overlays and waves, and reduced animation for those who need it.

- If the device has no WebGL, there is an alternative page that tells the story without 3D.

 

==========================================================================

3. WHAT MUST BE IN THE PRESENTATION

==========================================================================

3.1 Mandatory elements of the demo

According to last year's submission guide (confirm they are still the same in 2026):

- Team name and members.

- Chosen challenge: Dancing with the SARs.

- Project image.

- User experience.

- How the space data helped.

- Maximum 7 slides including the cover, in English, or a video of at most 30 seconds with English subtitles.

- Public link, no login.

 

3.2 Proposed 7 slides

 

# | SLIDE | CONTENT

---|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1 | Cover | Team name, members, challenge and image of the explorer

2 | The problem | The ground of the Mexicali Valley changes and cannot be seen at a glance. Cerro Prieto case

3 | The data | NISAR (NASA data), Copernicus DEM, WorldCover, WorldPop, OpenStreetMap. One line about the pipeline

4 | The solution | Screenshot of the explorer: flight, timeline and views

5 | User experience | A short walkthrough: choose a destination, move the date, tap the map, read the dashboard

6 | Finding and impact | Screenshot of Cerro Prieto with Accumulated or Rate, and people and land use in the zone. Use only values that the app shows

7 | Limits and future | The limits, one line each, next steps and credits

 

3.3 Messages worth repeating

- These are real radar measurements, not a simulation.

- The app points out patterns and exposure. The cause is studied separately.

- Anyone can understand the data without knowing radar.

 

==========================================================================

4. WHAT MUST NOT BE IN THE PRESENTATION

==========================================================================

TECHNICAL

- Code, function or file names, folders, tests or technologies (React, Three.js, TanStack, shadcn, openspec).

- Internal pipeline details (network inversion, deramp, unwrapping, coherence masks). One line is enough.

- Mentioning the synthetic mode. It is for development only and is not delivered.

 

CLAIMS THE DATA DOES NOT ALLOW

- Saying that geothermal or other activity causes the subsidence.

- Saying there is damage to houses, roads or crops.

- Presenting the movement in Accumulated or Rate as purely vertical. Radar measures along the line of sight and mixes vertical with horizontal.

- Presenting x2,000, x5,000 or x10,000 as the real subsidence.

- On crops: naming the crop, estimating harvest, saying that being close to water means irrigation, or using the 2021 coverage as if it were current.

- Saying the data is final (it is PROVISIONAL) or that one year of measurements is a long-term trend.

- Giving figures without mentioning the noise of +/-2 to 3 cm per date.

 

EVENT RULES

- NASA logos, flags or identifiers in the design.

- Personal or confidential information, product advertising, offensive language, names, voices or images of people under 18.

- More than 7 slides, or Spanish text in the demo.

- Third-party images or data without credit.

 

==========================================================================

5. HOW TO STATE THE LIMITS

==========================================================================

INSTEAD OF SAYING | SAY

------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------

"Geothermal activity sinks the ground" | "The ground is sinking around Cerro Prieto. The cause requires another study"

"This land dropped 12 cm" | "NISAR radar measures about 12 cm of change along the line of sight, with noise of +/-2 to 3 cm"

"These houses are damaged" | "This zone has this many people and this land use. It is exposure, not damage"

"The 3D subsidence shows reality" | "The relief is exaggerated to be visible. The data is in the layers"

"These crops will have a lower harvest" | "We show soil moisture and nearby water as context"

 

The example values are illustrative: replace them with the ones your app shows.

 

==========================================================================

6. PENDING TO CONFIRM

==========================================================================

- Dates, times and evaluation criteria of the Mexicali local event in 2026 (Judging and Awards guide).

- 2026 rules on artificial intelligence and NASA branding.

- Real Cerro Prieto values to be quoted on slide 6.

- Team name, members and final images.

- Where the demo will be hosted and that the link is public.
